title: Interleaved release-bridge for runtime/console/API cohorting
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: create a coordinated "release-bridge" plan to interleave runtime, Console, and API release trains so feature flighting and capacity ramps can be staged per-region with reduced risk.

Scope: produce a gated calendar, signals for go/no-go at each train boundary, a choreography for traffic shaping (shadow -> canary -> regional roll), and a lightweight ops runbook for week-of-launch burnboxes. Exclude model weight rollouts (handled in ENG runbook) and long-lived enterprise schedule negotiation (handled by sales ops).

Success metrics: 1) <20% of launches require rollback or mitigation within 72h; 2) cross-team coordination tasks completed in preflight within 5 working days; 3) no more than one SLA breach attributable to rollout scheduling per quarter.

Stakeholders: PM (Priya Nair), Runtime Eng (Elena Gomez), Console Eng (Omar Basu), SRE (Marcus Holt), Design (Sofia Martinez), GTM (Ruth Chang).

2026-03-01 Priya Nair: Updated calendar template and gating checklist. Added SLO guardrails and preflight owner checklist. Shared in #launch-conductor.
2026-03-05 Omar Basu (Console): Console dashboards require a temporary per-route view for release window, ETA two sprints. Filing ENG task ENG-33210 (dependency).
2026-03-09 Marcus Holt (SRE): Proposed burnbox staffing matrix and on-call rotation for week-of-launch. Recommend pairing with Dedicated capacity team for reserved slots.
2026-03-10 Priya Nair: Decided to pilot release-bridge on runtime-1.29 / console-2026.03 for Q2 feature slate. Next: finalize regional slices and run through tabletop rehearsal (target 2026-03-28).
notes: Trade-offs: tighter interleaving reduces latency to market but increases scheduling complexity and dependency surface. Decided to mitigate by requiring a preflight 'calendar freeze' of 72h and a single point of release ownership per train. Follow-ups: 1) create calendar-as-code template (owner: Infrastructure PM); 2) add automatic alerting for cross-train conflicts in Console (owner: Console Eng).
